building_valuation_fee.cite: FY26/27 MFS Building Fees p. 22 rows 1-8
building_valuation_fee.method: Row base plus $10.39 for each $1,000 of valuation above the row floor, prorated (not rounded up to the next $1,000), rounded to the cent half-to-even. Row 1 is a flat $179.67 up to $2,000. The City prints this table without saying how to handle a partial $1,000, and the published rows make the fee drop at the $1,000,000 and $5,000,000 boundaries. Treat the result as an estimate and confirm it with the Building Division.

planning_entitlement_fee_lines.note: Design Review Board / Planning Commission review. The board tier is not one fee — Minor, Board, Referral, and Major each have their own line, and Major is an actual-cost deposit, never a flat total.
Administrative (Director) Design Review — one adopted flat line.

Coastal Development Permit. The City's CDP Application (July 2026, p. 3) names the CDP type for each fee line: Administrative = Minor Development - Non-Appealable; Minor Appealable Zone = Minor Development - Appealable; Major Appealable Zone = Standard Development - Appealable; Non-Appealable Zone = Standard Development - Non-Appealable. Minor development is the LBMC 25.07.013 hearing waiver (consistent with the LCP, no other discretionary approval, no coastal effect). Standard development is every other CDP (LBMC 25.07.012). Decide three facts separately: ADU-only or not; any other discretionary approval; appeal area (site facts). Code 66329(c) makes it non-appealable. De minimis waiver, de minimis hearing and Approval in Concept apply only from a City record or a deferred-certification site fact. They differ on appealability. The 8-27-26 letter ("not appealable") governs: it is the later City statement on the same case; it matches the City appeal map (parcel field CDPAPPL = No); and it matches Gov. Code 66329(c). The 3-9-26 "appealable" sentence is a template error, not City practice. That work class may be the City's catch-all CDP case type. It does not change this rule.
CDP Exemption — one adopted flat line.
Revocable Encroachment Permit — one adopted flat line.
Lot Line Adjustment — one adopted flat line.

Conditional Use Permit. The schedule also carries Amendment, Intensification, Major Design Review, and Minor Design Review CUP lines; a residential review that needs one of those is outside this map and is a planner question.
